author: PTI_News
author_bio: India’s largest and most trusted news agency since 1949.
text:
STORY | Centre must ensure every road has encroachment-free space for walking: SC

The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Centre to ensure that wherever there is a road, there is a properly demarcated, encroachment-free space for pedestrians.

A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe asked Additional Solicitor General K M Nararaj, appearing for the Centre, to instruct the authorities concerned to make sure that the space meant for walking is not encroached upon and is properly separated from motor vehicle lanes.

"Without any big investment and construction, just ensure that proper demarcation is done of walkers' space. Wherever there is a road, there should be a walkers’ space. Do it with a rope or anything and ensure it is not encroached," the bench told Nataraj.

The bench gave him two weeks to instruct the authorities while emphasising that pedestrians should have confidence that the space is meant for them and they can walk freely without any threat of moving vehicles.

author: LtGovDelhi
author_bio: Official Twitter Account of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi
text:
Took a high-level review meeting of @MCD_Delhi to drive a comprehensive action plan for stronger urban governance, improved civic infrastructure, and enhanced structural safety across the capital.

Emphasized strict enforcement of building bylaws to curb illegal structural expansions and directed the MCD to implement a time-bound strategy to tackle unauthorized constructions decisively. Also reviewed key civic priorities, including desilting of stormwater drains ahead of the monsoon, road and pavement repairs for dust mitigation, and intensified garbage clearance to strengthen sanitation standards.

Reviewed public welfare initiatives, with a focus on expediting the PM-UDAY scheme for residents of unauthorized colonies and finalizing a participatory CSR framework for the rejuvenation of public parks.

Guided by Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji’s vision of inclusive development, our commitment remains to provide every Delhi resident with a safe, planned, clean, and dignified living environment.

Madam CM, please fix accountability of MCD & other agencies responsible for garbage collection. I have filed so many complaints on official portals. Either no action is taken or the complaint is marked “resolved” without any action on the ground. I have even emailed you. I get the standard response: “Forwarded to the concerned for necessary action" and then? Nothing.

People will not change just because we keep running cleanliness campaigns. You need strict penalties + zero tolerance for corruption + accountable departments.

Look at Singapore, Japan etc. People take pride in keeping their neighbourhoods clean because the system works and rules are enforced.

Make cleanliness a movement, yes. But first make accountability a movement within MCD and other agencies. Delhi needs action on the ground, not “resolved” complaints on a portal.

author: LtGovDelhi
author_bio: Official Twitter Account of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi
text:
Visited the @MCD_Delhi solid waste dump site at Bhalswa Landfill to review the progress of ongoing bioremediation efforts.

After Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji had flagged the three major garbage dump sites in Delhi—Bhalswa, Ghazipur, and Okhla Landfills—as “mountains of garbage” and called for their removal, work began in right earnest in 2022.

While significant progress has been made over the past year, much remains to be done.

Advised that the latest and emerging global technologies in waste management be explored, along with international benchmarks and expert consultation, to accelerate outcomes.

Directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to address not only legacy waste but also the continuous inflow of fresh waste at these sites.

Emphasized the urgent need to put in place all preventive measures to avoid fire incidents at the dump sites, especially with the onset of summer.

Also called upon the Municipal Corporation of Delhi to undertake a concerted effort to involve RWAs and MTAs across Delhi in ensuring segregation of waste at source into dry and wet categories, enabling faster and more effective bioremediation.

Interacted with workers on-site to understand their concerns and directed that all necessary health safeguards be ensured by the concessionaires.
